subject: Post-demo follow-up: inference ops interop & telemetry qualification playbook
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika.shah@cloudline.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Redwood / Cloudline inference ops — next steps

Hi Anika —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Useful conversation; I wanted to capture the follow-ups we agreed on and propose a lightweight ops/telemetry qualification playbook so your platform team can compare runtime observability and integration risk side-by-side with your hyperscaler evaluation.

Agreed follow-ups from the call:
- Redwood will hand over a short comparison matrix (attached) that lines up telemetry coverage (tracing, token-level metrics, prefix-cache visibility) vs Cloudline and a common hyperscaler baseline.
- Cloudline will share a concise list of their existing dashboards and retention policies.
- We’ll run a 48-hour side-by-side smoke test: sample load, streaming session traces, and billing/usage reconciliation.

Proposed playbook (high level):
1) Quick telemetry checklist (what to validate in the first 24h): streaming traces, per-request latency breakdown, token counts, KV cache hit rate, model fallback events.
2) Integration tests (24–48h): ingestion of traces into your APM, ingestion of token metrics into your billing pipeline, correlation IDs across edge -> runtime.
3) Outcome criteria: must surface per-token cost, per-session latency percentiles, and a match-rate on request IDs between systems for >=95% of sampled requests.

I attached the matrix + a starter dashboard proposal. Can you confirm those next steps and the people on your side who would run the smoke test? I’ll loop in Marissa (obs lead) and Ben (solutions) to coordinate tickets and any temporary access needed.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-cloudline-ops-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), telemetry-dashboard-proposal.pdf (PDF)

From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@cloudline.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: evan@embrace-ai.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood / Cloudline inference ops — next steps

Laura —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the matrix. Echoing what we said on the call: this is exactly the kind of tangible checklist we need to compare vendor telemetry and operational risk. I copied Evan (platform) who will own running the smoke test next week.

We can commit to running a 48-hour smoke test starting Tuesday (10/06) if you can provide temporary read-only credentials for your demo runtime and the sample request set. Also please include the expected schema for the token-level metrics (fields and units) so we can map into our billing pipeline.

We don’t want to block on long retention conversations — short-term we’ll accept a 7-day export of traces and token counts for the test window.

Anika
Head of Strategic Partnerships, Cloudline
Anika.Shah@cloudline.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood / Cloudline inference ops — next steps

Laura / Ben —

Nice. A few operational clarifications before we hand over creds and the sample set:

1) Sample set: please confirm we’ll use the same 10k-session replay set we used for the benchmarks in May (contains multi-turn chat, long-prefixs, and streaming calls). If Cloudline needs a smaller slice for faster onboarding, specify the session IDs.

2) Traces: We'll expose tracing spans with the following out-of-band headers: X-Request-ID, X-Session-ID, X-Model-Variant. Make sure Cloudline's platform can echo back X-Request-ID in any exported logs so we can match events.

3) Metrics schema (token-level): timestamp, request_id, tokens_generated, prompt_tokens, model_variant, latency_ms, kv_cache_hits. Attachments: I exported the matrix with a second tab that adds expected JSON schemas.

4) Security: Temporary creds will be scoped and rotated after 3 days. No PII in the sample set; privacy watermarking already applied.

Next actions I’ll take:
- Share the sample tar and temporary account by Monday EOD (10/05).
- Create a short Jira board for the smoke test and invite Cloudline.

Ben — can you prepare the lightweight dashboard that maps token metrics -> cost and surface the two KPIs Anika asked for (per-token cost & 95th latency)? I’ll attach a minimal Grafana JSON export.

Marissa
Observability Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: demo-logs-20260930.tar.gz

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood / Cloudline inference ops — next steps

On it — will build a pared-down Grafana dashboard and provide a JSON export. Key panels I’ll include:
- Per-session latency (p50/p95/p99) broken down by model variant
- Token generation rate over time (tokens/sec) with overlayed model-engine selection events
- KV cache hit rate by prefix length buckets
- Cost estimator: simple formula (tokens_generated * unit_cost[model_variant]) with toggle for batching assumptions

I’ll drop the Grafana JSON and a short README with instructions for importing into Cloudline’s Grafana instance. ETA: Monday 10/05 lunchtime.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood / Cloudline inference ops — next steps

Anika —

Thanks — confirming we’ll start the smoke test on Tuesday 2026-10-06. Deliverables from Redwood by 10/05 EOD (PST):
- Temporary read-only creds and a scoped S3 drop with the sample replay (demo-logs-20260930.tar.gz)
- redwood-cloudline-ops-matrix.xlsx with the telemetry schema tab
- Grafana JSON + README (Ben)
- Short Jira board and test plan (Marissa)

Success criteria reminder for Cloudline ops team to validate during the 48-hour run:
- Trace correlation: >=95% request ID match between Redwood traces and Cloudline exports
- Observability completeness: ability to reconstruct per-session latency and token counts for sampled requests
- Cost mapping: token-level data can be mapped to a unit-price estimate (we’ll share our unit costs in the matrix)

If any of your platform folks need a pre-check, Sergio can run a quick health-check of the exported traces to ensure headers are present.

Looking forward to the results — I’ll post the HubSpot activity and link the Jira board once created.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Forwarded attachments: redwood-cloudline-ops-matrix.xlsx, telemetry-dashboard-proposal.pdf, demo-logs-20260930.tar.gz
